scope.mode: read-only source review plus immutable report blob

conclusion.refreshTarget: the host-configured fixed MIKKA_CLOUD_WORKER_SOURCE_COMMIT and MIKKA_CLOUD_WORKER_SHA, not a newly published npm version or an app commit chosen by inference
conclusion.summary: Fresh instances of the configured additive Rfacb/Wa453 image start its built/preloaded worker. Publishing a newer public npm daemon does not update that cloud worker. Current host code can explicitly refresh an idle task, or upgrade an eligible retained idle/unclaimed task during its legitimate next start when its worker fingerprint differs from the configured target. The actual running worker identity must be established from the real release/task evidence; a template/configuration witness and Native CI installed daemon are not that evidence.

publicWitness.providedBy: root message, existing public Factory progress witness
publicWitness.boundary: This review did not fetch the live configuration or the manifest artifact and did not inspect the running sandbox. The witness does not independently prove a live worker PID, cwd, compiled source, refreshed release or actual npm version.

identityContract.meaning: fixed public Git source commit used to build the cloud worker
worker fingerprint from immutable relevant Git entries (including mode/type/blob/path) and package/lock projections
identityContract.boundary: W was not recomputed against R in this source-only review; the supplied W remains the release witness identity.

identityContract.meaning: host application source is a separate identity; the reviewed selection/build/refresh checks do not require AppSHA == R
public desktop/service package version is not the E2B cloud-worker release selector

findings.detail: Template construction fetches and verifies exact R, recomputes the required worker fingerprint, installs the filtered locked dependencies, compiles dist/cloud/cloud-worker.js with W and freezes an anonymous preloaded worker. The cloud worker is not installed from the public npm latest release.

Install mode seeing an existing worker marker requires that marker to equal requested W and returns. It does not overwrite an old installation. Stage mode is a separate guarded path. The install early-return proves the marker check, not a new live-process verification.

start-prebuilt.sh executes the bundled worker under /opt/mikka/worker; the normal start command wakes its existing --wait-bootstrap process or starts the bundle (legacy fallback is the same checkout's local tsx entry). Neither command downloads a new npm daemon.

findings.status: proved in immutable Rfacb, and identical entry/CLI/updater bytes directly read at main e189
findings.detail: cloud-worker invokes runCli with --hosted-subscriptions and --e2b-container-runtime. The CLI excludes either flag from managedAutoUpdateRuntime enabled eligibility. The updater separately requires prod, systemd/launchd and the actual public global npm mikka.js install. R's main may learn the server-named newer version but offer/install and daemon.update remain unavailable without options.autoUpdate.

findings.status: proved at candidate932; schema directly identical at main e189
findings.detail: Task harness selects E2B_CLAUDE_TEMPLATE or E2B_CODEX_TEMPLATE; Bot/desktop selects E2B_BYO_COMPUTER_TEMPLATE. Bare official kind is the supported bootstrap/rollback route. Additive IDs must match the strict configured catalogue, kind and preinstalled flag. Catalogue W and optional R are checked against the corresponding host configuration. The selector does not query the latest npm daemon.

findings.status: proved in candidate932 host source, same blob as e189 search binding
findings.detail: Fresh provision/ordinary verification compares the sandbox/broker's W with the configured target. A mismatch outside authorized refresh/retained-upgrade eligibility is rejected. Existing running question/claimed work has preservation paths and is not forcibly migrated; this is not a claim that every already active child rechecks the latest W on every call.

findings.status: proved in candidate932 host source, same blob as e189 search binding
findings.detail: Explicit refresh_runtime requires an existing owned official task machine and terminal/idle eligibility. A legitimate next start may also upgrade a retained queued task or an unclaimed question when source W differs from configured W. The code preserves original VM/task/session ownership, requires idle/no competing active runs, stages fixed configured R/W, switches under owner policy/claim locks and lease checks, revokes superseded device tokens, then starts/registers and verifies the replacement process. This is a real automatic-on-eligible-start exception to 'never refresh', but it is not npm auto-update.

findings.status: existing implementation, not executed by this review
findings.detail: The refresh verifier binds trusted worker marker W and the release symlink R, checks live PID/cwd/cloud-worker argv/user, and after a switch rejects a process predating it. The host also verifies daemon.status belongs to that PID/device/workspace and requires fresh registration before finishing. Marker or declared catalogue alone is weaker than this existing process evidence.

runtimeCases.case: Fresh configured additive image remains Rfacb/Wa453
runtimeCases.outcome: uses old R-built/preloaded worker; newer npm publication alone has no effect
bootstrap fetches/builds the configured fixed R/W, not latest npm
idempotent bootstrap exits; no source upgrade implied

runtimeCases.case: Existing ordinary start with W mismatch and no eligible refresh
runtimeCases.outcome: fails the worker version guard rather than silently replacing source

runtimeCases.case: Eligible retained idle task or unclaimed question, configured target W changed
runtimeCases.outcome: normal lifecycle may stage/switch to the configured fixed release under existing guards; only actual success receipts prove it happened

runtimeCases.case: Explicit refresh_runtime on owned eligible idle task
Already claimed or live question/native child
runtimeCases.outcome: preservation paths do not establish automatic migration to a new worker; no force-upgrade inference

minimumActualEvidencePath.purpose: Establish which worker supplied the real acceptance run; reuse existing release/runtime/task evidence, not a new AppSHA == R gate or an additional model run.
configuration: existing accepted release R and W
selected per-kind template IDs and catalogue consistency across the existing six configuration keys
taskBinding: the actual case's selected template provenance / retained-machine branch
the actual worker W used by the normal bootstrap/registration path
processBinding: where the runtime was refreshed, the existing verified_process receipt and matching daemon.status/registration result
R, W and process identity must describe the same actual worker; omit device/workspace/token values from a public summary
minimumActualEvidencePath.coverageDecision: Use the separate 27-daemon-path source review to decide whether that actual worker contains the tracing/generation fixes needed by this case. This review does not independently audit or reclassify that diff.
minimumActualEvidencePath.ifEvidenceMissing: Keep actual worker identity unknown. Do not fill it with Native installedRevision, npm release metadata, template name alone, or the host app SHA.
minimumActualEvidencePath.noNewRequirement: No arbitrary application/runtime SHA equality, template rebuild requirement, extra CLI/model run, new threshold or new account gate is introduced.

sourceBoundary.note: Rfacb's host thread-machines source differs from e189/932; the current server-side selection/refresh conclusion is bound to the latter. The old cloud worker's no-npm-update conclusion is independently bound to Rfacb's worker/CLI/updater. No assertion that all three complete source trees are identical.
